sections.h2: West Valley City at a glance
sections.html:
West Valley City is an inner suburb on the northwest side of the Salt Lake Valley and the second most populous city in Utah. Salt Lake City is to its north, South Salt Lake to the east, Magna to the west, and Taylorsville and Kearns to the south. The Oquirrh Mountains are west and the Jordan River forms the eastern edge. It covers roughly 35.5 to 35.9 square miles at about 4,304 feet.

The city incorporated in 1980 by merging four unincorporated communities: Hunter, Granger, Chesterfield and Redwood. It had 72,299 people in 1980, 129,480 in 2010 and 140,230 in 2020, an 8.3% rise over the last decade. The July 2025 estimate at the top of this page is 137,491, a little below the 2020 count.

sections.h2: Areas of the city and their houses
sections.html:
The city is usually described in three areas, and the age of the houses differs among them. These descriptions rest on 2013 neighborhood data, so incomes and populations have shifted since.

  • East (Redwood, Chesterfield and East Granger): mostly brick ranch houses from the 1960s and 1970s, near Valley Fair Mall and the Maverik Center. The Westshire area south of the mall has 160 mid-century modern homes from the 1960s and 1970s.
  • Central (West Granger and Hunter south of 3100 South, with Lakepark and Westlake Business Park to the north): includes the planned Highbury development in the northwest portion.
  • West (West Hunter, Woodhaven and Oquirrh): mostly planned developments from the 1990s and 2000s.

Median household income in 2013 was $42,512 in the East, $55,087 in the Central area and $64,356 in the West. A seller in the East is often selling a 50 or 60 year old brick ranch, so roof, plumbing and electrical updates drive the price.

Interstate 215, State Route 172 (5600 West) and State Route 171 (3500 South) are the main roads. West Valley Central station is on the TRAX Green Line, and the Utah Transit Authority runs an intermodal hub in the city. The 3500 South MAX bus line serves the area, and the Midvalley Express links West Valley Central and 2700 West to Taylorsville and on to Murray Central station.

The Granite School District covers the city and serves about 67,000 students across central Salt Lake County. Granger High School, which opened in 1958, and Hunter High School, which opened in 1990, are both in West Valley City. Charter schools include East Hollywood High School, American Preparatory Academy and Monticello Academy. A school boundary depends on the address, so ask the district to confirm it before you advertise the house.

Every owner of a rental dwelling in West Valley City must hold a current city business license. An owner with several units needs only one license if they give the city a complete, current list of the units and pay the fees. When a property has more than one owner, each is jointly and severally liable for the fees and any penalties.

The code also sets a rental nuisance standard: more than two police calls for one rental unit in 12 months counts as excessive. An unresolved notice of violation is one with no recorded notice of compliance. The city's ordinance enforcement division handles abatement of unsightly or hazardous property and rental licensing.

  • Confirm your rental license is current before listing.
  • Clear any open notice of violation and record the notice of compliance.
  • Gather the unit list if you own more than one rental in the city.

sections.h2: Property tax in Salt Lake County
sections.html:
The county wants its property tax by November 30, and anything still unpaid on December 1 is delinquent. Notices come by November 1. The appeal window lasts 45 days and runs from August 1 to September 15. In late May the county sells parcels that are more than five years delinquent.

With Utah's 45% residential exemption, a primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value. A second residence or vacant house is taxed at the full amount, which is worth checking if you have already moved out.

The place to file is the Salt Lake County Recorder, 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, and the flat fee is $40.00. Include the parcel number and the grantee's mailing address, and have the deed notarized. That same office holds the ownership records the city checks when it identifies an owner for code and licensing.

After closing, the title company normally files the deed. For an inherited house, bring the old deed to the title company so the chain of ownership is clear before the sale.

sections.h2: Weather and wear on older houses
sections.html: Salt Lake City, the nearest long-term station, averages a July high of 94.0 degrees and a January high of 38.6, with about 15.5 inches of precipitation and strong winter inversions. That climate keeps steady wear on roofs and on heating and cooling systems, and it shows most in houses that are decades old. An inspector will check the roof, the furnace and air conditioner, the electrical panel and the plumbing, and each one can become a point in price talks.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or a tenant
sections.html:
Owing property tax does not stop a sale, since the title company takes the balance out of your proceeds and splits the current year's tax with the buyer. Still, do not let it slide. Five or more years of delinquency can put a parcel in the May tax sale, and options narrow fast by then.

For a rental, buyers will ask about the license, the unit list and any earlier notice of violation, so settle those items first. A tenant in place can slow a regular listing, because showings need notice and some buyers want to move in. A cash buyer can often close around the lease or after the tenant leaves. Raise it when you request an offer.

sections.h2: Selling a West Valley City house
sections.html:
You have three paths: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer. Listing suits a house in good shape and a seller willing to sit through showings. A cash sale suits an older ranch needing updates, a rental with code problems, or an inherited house nobody wants to look after.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses here as they stand. Ask for an offer, look at how we reached it, and make your own call. Keep the deed, the latest tax notice and any rental license handy to save time. We can set the closing date around your move, and the title company handles the deed filing and the tax split.

faqs.q: What county is West Valley City in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. Its offices in Salt Lake City handle the tax bill, valuation appeals and recording of deeds.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in West Valley City?
faqs.a: The due date is November 30, and a balance still unpaid on December 1 is delinquent. Notices are mailed by November 1.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent out a house in West Valley City?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of rental dwelling units must hold a current city business license, and multi-unit owners can use one license with a list of units.

faqs.q: Which school district serves West Valley City?
faqs.a: The Granite School District. Granger High School and Hunter High School are in the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Valley City house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses sell as-is all the time, and owners of older ranches often choose a cash sale so they skip repair bills before closing.
